messages:
alex: Heads up — during the 10:30 canary we saw ~3% of traffic still routed to v1 even though the rollout shows 97/3 split. Noticing stickiness to the old instance id. anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:
maya: hmm. which guard did you use? header-based or cookie-affinity?
alex: cookie-affinity with fallback to header.user-id. Config snippet: ```json
{
  "split": [
    {"version": "v2", "weight": 97},
    {"version": "v1", "weight": 3}
  ],
  "affinity": ["cookie:session_id", "header:X-User-ID", "ip"]
}
```
maya: can you paste the raw request/response headers from a routed-to-v1 case?
alex: pasted example below. note the Set-Cookie is present but path=/api/v1 not /, and the request had `x-user-id: 0` sometimes.
--- request ---
GET /complete 200 OK
Host: api.internal
X-User-ID: 0
X-Forwarded-Proto: https
Cookie: session_id=abc123; path=/api/v1
--- response ---
Set-Cookie: session_id=abc123; Path=/api/v1; HttpOnly
---
sam: :eyes: path=/api/v1 seems suspect. our affinity cookie code expects Path=/ (we normalize to root when computing cookie fingerprint). If path differs we strip it and fall back to header hashing.
jordan: also noticed in the rollout logs that our header normalization recently switched to lower-case canonicalization but some proxies send `X-User-Id` vs `X-User-ID`. The fallback list is case-sensitive in the hashing lookup by mistake.
priya: oh wow. so requests without normalized header end up skipping header-based affinity and go to deterministic hashing based on client ip -> that could bias towards older hosts in certain regions.
alex: telemetry: I'm seeing a cluster of hits from a region where client IPs hash to the same bucket, and because cookie lookup failed due to path mismatch they hit the fallback. attached small histogram: 92% of fallback hits land on v1.
maya: could the console rollout UI be saving header keys with mixed case? I remember a recent change to allow freeform header spec.
sam: yeah console stores them as-entered and the routing layer expects a normalized list. Fix options: (A) normalize headers on save in Console, (B) make routing lookup case-insensitive, (C) canonicalize cookie paths when setting them in app. We should do B + C short-term.
jordan: agreed. B is smallest blast radius. I'll open a patch to compare lower(header) when checking affinity.
priya: I'll fix the cookie writer in the app templates to set Path=/ by default so future responses don't create mismatched cookies.
alex: quick mitigation: can we force-enable ignore-cookie-path in the routing config for this canary so it treats session_id regardless of path?
maya: yep we have a per-rollout override flag `affinity.cookie.ignore_path` — we can flip it for the canary. But need approval (enterprise constraints).
priya: approve from my side for the canary window.
jordan: deploy-bot: rolling patch to routing (case-insensitive header lookup) to canary pool now.
deploy-bot: deploy started for commit sha: 5d3f9c, target: canary routing nodes (10%) — logs: https://ci/repo/5d3f9c
sam: post-deploy, I'll run a sweep comparing bucket assignment before/after and scrub telemetry for the affected region.
alex: thanks. I'll flip `affinity.cookie.ignore_path=true` for the canary and monitor. If we still see >1% misroute we rollback.
maya: note for postmortem: console UX should validate header keys and show normalization warning. Also add a small tooltip explaining cookie path implications for affinity.
priya: logging todo: emit when cookie path != "/" and affinity is enabled so we can alert automatically.
jordan: opened PR: https://git/repo/pulls/678 — adds lowercasing for header keys + tests.
sam: running canary health checks now. preliminary: misroute rate dropped from 3.1% -> 0.2% after the override + deploy.
alex: great. leaving this thread open for 1hr to watch metrics, then we'll close and file a short incident note. :thumbsup:
